findings.message: 'TIMEZONE' is not a grok pattern. Logstash refuses to compile an unknown name, so the filter never registers and EVERY line fails to parse - not just the ones this capture touches. Use a defined pattern: NUMBER or BASE10NUM for a decimal, HOSTNAME for a domain, NOTSPACE for anything without a space.

the extraction produced keys on 0 of 9 sample line(s). none of the patterns matches any sample line. The closest to the first line is '^\\[(?<timestamp>%{TIMESTAMP_ISO8601} %{TIMEZONE})\\] \\[%{INT:pid}/%{NOTSPACE:thread}\\] \\[%{LOGLEVEL:level}\\] (?<action>Su': the pattern matches up to %{INT:pid}, which fails on '[2026-10-30 19:03:22 +0000] [1/Thread-2 '. That position does not hold a bare number. Until this is right, every field is empty however it is mapped.
